title: 들은 말에 반응하기: 결혼한다니! 결혼한다면서?
objective: By the end, you can say you are surprised by news you just heard (-다니), check news you heard earlier (-는다면서), and ask what someone else said (-는다니?), with the right form for verbs, adjectives, nouns and the past.
summary: Learn three endings for reacting to things you hear: -다니 for surprise, -는다면서 for checking news you heard before, and -는다니? for asking what someone said.

task.title: Choose and write the ending
task.line: Read each situation, decide if it is new news, old news, or a question about what someone said, then write or choose the correct form.

forms.when: You just heard surprising news and repeat it back. 먹다 → 먹는다니, 그만두다 → 그만둔다니. Add -요 to be polite.
forms.means: Surprise or disbelief: "You're saying...? I can't believe it."

forms.when: Adjectives add -다니 straight to the stem. For the past, use -었다니 / -았다니.
forms.means: Surprise at a fact you just heard or saw.
forms.example: 방이 이렇게 좁다니! 사진하고 완전히 달라요.
forms.exampleMeaning: The room is this small? It looks nothing like the photos.

forms.when: After a noun, use -이라니 after a consonant and -라니 after a vowel.
forms.exampleMeaning: The exam is tomorrow? Wasn't it next week?

forms.when: You heard something before, from someone else or online, and now you check it with the person you are talking to (the news can be about them or about someone else, e.g. 민수가 결혼한다면서?).
forms.exampleMeaning: I heard you're getting married next month. Congratulations!

forms.when: Same use as above. Adjective: 바쁘다면서, past: 아팠다면서, noun: 생일이라면서.
forms.exampleMeaning: I heard you were really sick yesterday. Are you OK now?

forms.when: Casual speech (반말) only. You ask the listener what a third person told them.
forms.exampleMeaning: What time did Dad say he's coming home today?

watchOut: 바쁜다니 (X) → 바쁘다니 (O): Adjectives never take -ㄴ다 / -는다. Add -다니 and -다면서 straight to the stem.
의사다니 (X) → 의사라니 (O): After a noun, use -(이)라니 and -(이)라면서.
만들는다면서 (X) → 만든다면서 (O): For verbs ending in ㄹ, drop the ㄹ and add -ㄴ다.
A: 나 이사해. B: 이사한다면서? (X) → 이사한다니! (O): If you are hearing the news for the first time right now, use -다니. -는다면서 is only for news you heard earlier.
팀장님, 사장님은 언제 오신다니? (X) → 팀장님, 사장님은 언제 오신대요? (O): -는다니? is casual only and has no -요 form for this meaning. When you speak politely, use -는대요?.
exercises: Your friend tells you this right now. Choose the right word: A: 나 다음 주에 미국으로 유학 가. B: 갑자기 유학을 (간다니 / 간다면서)! 왜 이제 말해?
Change the word in brackets to the -다니 form: ① 4월인데 날씨가 이렇게 ____! (춥다) ② 그 조용한 사람이 ____! (가수이다) ③ 내일 파티에서 쓸 케이크를 직접 ____! (만들다)
Yesterday your team leader told you that 하준 is moving to Busan. Today you meet 하준. Use -는다면서요: 하준 씨, 부산으로 ____? (이사하다)
Your friend just finished a phone call with 민호. Ask your friend what 민호 said. Use -는다니?: 민호는 몇 시에 ____? (도착하다)
Find the mistake and correct it: 그 식당이 그렇게 맛있는다면서요?
Choose the right word: ① A friend told you last week that Mina's birthday is next week. You see Mina: 다음 주가 (생일이라니요 / 생일이라면서요)? ② Mina then says, "사실 저 다음 달에 한국을 떠나요.": 벌써 (떠난다니요 / 떠난다면서요)?
answers: ① 춥다니 ② 가수라니 ③ 만든다니
